connections.name: Update check
connections.sends: a request for the newest version: no identifier, your IP address as any request shows it
connections.whileOff: you check for new versions yourself, with Check now or on the download page
connections.detail: Once you turn it on, the app asks deusneuma.ai/updates/ shortly after launch and every 30 minutes whether a newer version exists and, when one does, fetches its signature. The request carries no account, key or install identifier; like any download, the site sees your IP address and which file was asked for, which tells it the app's version and system. If our release key signed the update, the AppImage downloads it, and the .deb and .rpm tell you; otherwise nothing downloads. While it is off, the app asks nothing unless you press Check now.

connections.name: Security watch
connections.sends: the names and versions of the libraries the app ships, and of any project you add to the watch
connections.whileOff: the daily watch still runs on this computer, without the online check for known flaws
connections.detail: Once you turn it on, the app asks the public OSV vulnerability database (api.osv.dev, run by Google) once a day whether any library it ships has a known flaw. It sends the names and versions of those libraries, the same for every install of this version, and of the libraries in any project folder you add to the watch. No identifier is sent; OSV sees your IP address. While it is off, the daily watch still runs on your machine and sends nothing.

connections.name: Public platform data
connections.when: when a neuma reads public figures
connections.sends: anonymous requests for public figures from Umbrae, an Ignis platform
connections.whileOff: a neuma cannot read Umbrae's public figures
connections.detail: Once you turn it on, a neuma may read public platform figures from umbrae.io, a sister Ignis AI Labs product, without asking you each time, with anonymous requests that carry nothing about you; umbrae.io sees your IP address. While it is off, nothing is asked of it.

connections.name: House mailbox watch
connections.to: the mail server you connected for the house mailbox
connections.sends: the house mailbox's sign-in, to list the newest messages read-only
connections.whileOff: new mail waits until a being or you check the mailbox
connections.detail: Once you turn it on, every 5 minutes the app signs in to the mail server you connected for the house mailbox and lists the newest messages, read-only: it marks nothing read and sends nothing. A new message from an investor or a lead the house is talking to wakes the seat that holds that conversation; any other new message wakes the being that holds the mailbox. Every wake stays inside your house charter. Your mail provider sees the sign-in from this computer, as it does when you check mail yourself. While it is off, the house reads mail only when a being checks it.

connections.name: Sanctions list
connections.to: treasury.gov (the US Treasury's public sanctions list)
connections.when: once a day, while the legal watch runs
connections.sends: a request for the public list: no identifier, your IP address as any request shows it
connections.whileOff: buyers and investors are not screened, and the legal office says so
connections.detail: Once you turn it on, the legal office downloads the US Treasury's public sanctions list (the Specially Designated Nationals list and its other names, from treasury.gov) at most once a day and keeps it on this computer. It checks the names of the house's buyers and investors against that copy here; no name ever leaves your machine. The request carries no account or identifier; the Treasury's site sees your IP address. A match is only a possible match, filed for you and your CLO to look at. While it is off, nothing is screened.

connections.name: Chats with the house
connections.to: Telegram's and Discord's servers, through the bots you connected
connections.when: all the time while on: Telegram is asked for new messages every 25 seconds, Discord holds one open line
connections.sends: your bots' tokens, to hear the messages sent to them, and the answers of the beings who hold them
connections.whileOff: your bots post what you approve, but hear nobody
connections.detail: Once you turn it on, each Telegram and Discord bot you connected for the house, and gave a holder, listens for messages sent to it. A person you approve can then talk with the being who holds that bot, in a direct chat, or in a group you approved when the message names the bot. A stranger only gets a pairing code back, and nothing they send is read until you approve that code (WAITING ON YOU, or the platform's CHATS tab). Telegram and Discord see what is sent and answered, as with any chat on their services. While it is off, the bots only post what you approve.

connections.name: The web
connections.to: the search index and the pages a neuma reads
connections.when: on by default; each time, once you approve it (or allow always, or use AUTO)
connections.sends: a neuma's searches, page reads, and the links of the videos and recordings it watches or listens to
connections.detail: When a neuma searches or reads the web, the query and the pages it reads leave your machine. Searches always go to DuckDuckGo, and also to Exa, Brave or your own SearXNG once you add a key or address for them. If you save a Cloudflare token, a page that needs a browser to read is fetched through Cloudflare's page-reading service, which receives its address. Each search or page asks for your approval first, unless you allow a neuma always or chat in AUTO mode. When a neuma watches a video or listens to a recording from a link, yt-dlp fetches it from the site it is on, through a door on this computer that reaches only the internet, never this computer or your network; that site sees your IP address and which recording was asked for, as it would if you played it. Each watch asks for your approval like a page read. Turning web access off in Settings stops a neuma's web search, page reading and watching.

connections.name: Cloud models
connections.sends: what is said to that model, under its provider's terms
connections.detail: A neuma always runs on a model on your own machine; the app refuses to route a neuma through a cloud provider. You can add a cloud model, from about 150 providers, as a witness, in a council or to run the harness. Choosing a provider asks it for its list of models, so it sees your IP address; once you add your key or sign in (OpenAI, GitHub Copilot and xAI sign in through their own pages), what is said to that model goes to its provider, under its terms. Your conversations stay on your disk as well.

connections.name: Wallets
connections.to: a public Ethereum node and CoinGecko
connections.when: when you open a wallet, or every 10 minutes once you save your own node
connections.sends: your wallet address, to read it; prices are asked with coin names, never an address
connections.detail: Your wallet's balances and transactions are read and sent through a public Ethereum node (ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com, or one you set), which sees your wallet address. A neuma's own wallet is read through Base's public node (mainnet.base.org), which sees that wallet's address. The wallet view asks CoinGecko for prices with coin names only, never an address. If you save your own node address, the app checks every 10 minutes for payments received by your house's and your neumas' wallets.

connections.name: Sealing
connections.sends: an encrypted record, your address and signatures, permanently
connections.detail: Sealing a birth is done on this computer by default: the being and you each sign its birth record, and nothing leaves your machine. Writing the seal to Ethereum as well is a public, permanent transaction, made only if you choose it: an encrypted record, your address and your signatures are written to the chain for good. Opening that choice reads your wallet's balance from a public Ethereum node and the price of ETH from CoinGecko, to show what it costs.

connections.name: Legal research
connections.to: public legal databases, the pages it cites, and regulators' feeds
connections.when: once you seat a legal officer
connections.sends: the question a neuma is researching, the addresses of the pages it cites, and its search terms
connections.detail: A neuma you seat as your house's legal officer may query public US legal databases (Congress.gov, GovInfo, Regulations.gov, CourtListener, Open States) with the question it is researching, without asking you each time. Before its readings and opinions are recorded, the app also opens again every page it cites, to check that the quoted words and headings are really there, and searches official sources (the Federal Register, legislation.gov.uk, and the SEC, CFTC, FTC, FCA, ESMA and EDPB news feeds) for anything from the last 120 days on its search terms. These reads go only to those public sites and carry no account or identifier; each site sees your IP address. Turning web access off in Settings stops them. Until you seat a legal officer, nothing is asked.

connections.name: Second legal reader
connections.when: only if you choose a connected provider as your legal officer's second reader
connections.sends: each claim your legal officer cites, with the passage of law it rests on
connections.detail: Before your legal officer's opinions and readings are recorded, a second reader checks each cited passage against the claim it is cited for. By default that reader is your house's own model on this computer, and nothing leaves your machine. If you choose one of your connected providers instead, in the LEGAL window, each claim and the passage of law it rests on go to that provider, under its terms. A provider on this computer's own key can only be chosen by its owner. Choose the house's own model again to stop.

connections.name: Channels and remote access
connections.sends: what you approve to post, and reads of your posts' stats and replies
connections.detail: Social channels (X, Telegram, Discord, Facebook, LinkedIn, Mastodon, Bluesky), email (your own mail server) and remote access (your own relay, your Tailscale network or your local network; there is no Ignis relay) talk only to the services you connect, and only once you do. Once a channel is connected, the app posts what you approved at its time, checks X for replies every 10 minutes, and reads the likes, replies and views of the posts you sent on X, Bluesky and Facebook every 30 minutes. If you save a Deus Neuma site token, it asks deusneuma.ai for your links' visit counts every 6 hours, with that token. A Hugging Face token you save is handed only to the local engines you run.

connections.name: Downloads you start
connections.when: only when you press a download, set up an engine or a model, or a neuma first watches or listens to something
connections.sends: a request for the file, like any download: your IP address and which file was asked for (and your Hugging Face token to Hugging Face, if you saved one)
connections.detail: Setting up the model server downloads Ollama, or the llama.cpp engine, from their releases on GitHub, and the model from Hugging Face. Setting up dictation downloads whisper.cpp from its releases on GitHub (on Linux, with an NVIDIA graphics card that has room for it, the graphics-card build from Deus Neuma's own releases on GitHub) and its speech model from Hugging Face. Every engine, and every model the app downloads itself, is checked against its pinned size and SHA-256 before it is used; a model pulled through Ollama is checked by Ollama's own digests. The first time a neuma watches a video or listens to a recording, the app downloads yt-dlp from its releases on GitHub and, on a computer without ffmpeg, a static ffmpeg build from GitHub, each checked the same way; when a site changes how it serves video, yt-dlp updates itself from its GitHub releases, checking the update against its publisher's signature, at most once every six hours. A recording without captions sets up speech recognition as dictation would, if it is not set up. Nothing here downloads on its own, and no install identifier is sent.
